summary: The Skyway Code explains the UK GA weather products. The F215 forecasts weather below 10,000 ft for a 9-hour period, the F214 gives upper winds and temperatures, and the GAMET is a plain-text low-level forecast issued four times a day for four UK regions. TAFs are forecasts and METARs are reports, with cloud heights above aerodrome level. A ceiling is BKN or OVC, and legal VFR minima are limits, not targets. Built from the Skyway Code pp.33-40.
src: The Skyway Code (CAP 1535 v4, Nov 2023), pp.33-40
sections: F215, F214 and GAMET
F215 forecasts in-flight weather below 10,000 ft for the British Isles over a 9-hour period centred on a fixed time. F415 is the near-Europe version

The F215 shows fronts and pressure centres at the chart time, zones lettered A, B, C with cloud amount, type and heights above mean sea level, visibility, ice and turbulence, and the freezing level (0°C isotherm). XXX means tops above the chart limit
F214 gives forecast upper winds and temperatures at 'spot' positions (columns: altitude in 1,000s of feet, wind direction, speed, temperature). F414 is near Europe
GAMET is an abbreviated plain-text low-level forecast issued four times a day for four UK regions. It replaced AIRMETs and includes the synoptic summary, hazards, freezing level and zone forecasts
Reading TAFs and METARs
TAFs are forecasts, METARs are reports of actual weather, normally updated every half hour
Example: 34008KT is wind from 340° at 8 kt. 9999 means visibility 10 km or more. SCT025 is 3 to 4 oktas at 2,500 ft above aerodrome level (AAL)
Cloud type is not reported unless it is cumulonimbus or towering cumulus
TEMPO is a temporary change within a period. PROB30 and PROB40 are the only probabilities used in the UK. If PROB30/40 or uncertain timings appear, look at the overall situation more thoroughly
Cloud is given above the aerodrome, so compare with terrain on your route. A 1,500 ft ceiling can hide hill tops
Viewing reports on a map helps build the weather picture. A SIGMET warns of severe weather such as thunderstorms, mountain waves, icing or turbulence
Icing in the Skyway Code
If you enter visible moisture at 0°C or below, airframe ice may form. The worst usually occurs between 0°C and -15°C
Always remove frost, ice and snow, and keep the pitot and static ports clear
Carb ice comes from the pressure and temperature drop in the venturi. It often forms outside visible moisture with high humidity and is more likely at low power
The carb icing risk chart plots dewpoint against air temperature and shows serious icing at any power or at descent power, so use carb heat per the AFM
Fuel-injected engines can still ice at the air intake: use alternate air
Making the weather decision
Know the conditions linked with warm and cold fronts, high and low pressure and thunderstorms
Cloud ceiling is the lowest cloud covering more than half the sky (BKN or OVC). Cloud base is the lowest visible cloud and includes FEW and SCT
Legal VFR minima are limits, not targets. Class G can allow 1,500 m visibility clear of cloud but the cloud height often forces dangerously low flight
Ceiling of 1,500 ft AGL or less needs particular attention to terrain. Below 1,000 ft AGL is normally for circuits or familiar local flying
Surface visibility under 5 km is not recommended for VFR: the horizon is unlikely to be clear. Haze towards the sun and low winter sun can reduce visibility
Winds above about 35 kt aloft often mean bumpy conditions, and strong headwinds affect fuel
If you do not hold an IR or IMC rating, you must not enter cloud

cards.q: What period does an F215 cover?
cards.a: A 9-hour period centred on a fixed time, below 10,000 ft.

cards.q: How often is a GAMET issued?
cards.a: Four times a day for four UK regions.

cards.q: What does XXX on the F215 mean?
cards.a: Cloud tops above the chart upper limit.

cards.q: What is the difference between a TAF and a METAR?
cards.a: A TAF is a forecast, a METAR is a report of the actual weather.

cards.q: Cloud heights in TAFs and METARs are measured from where?

cards.a: A temporary condition within the stated period.

cards.q: Which probabilities are used in UK TAFs?

cards.a: A warning of severe weather such as thunderstorms, mountain waves, icing or turbulence.
The lowest cloud covering more than half the sky (BKN or OVC).

quiz.why: BKN or OVC forms a ceiling. FEW and SCT do not.

quiz.q: A METAR reports visibility as 9999. This means:
quiz.why: 9999 is used for 10 km or more.

quiz.q: The Skyway Code says legal VFR visibility minima should be regarded as:
quiz.why: Safe VFR flight normally ceases long before the legal minima.

quiz.q: Which product is a plain-text forecast issued four times a day for low-level GA?
quiz.why: GAMET replaced AIRMET and covers four UK regions.
